newsitem.title: INDIA: India raises retail sugar sale price.
newsitem.headline: India raises retail sugar sale price.

text.p: India on Monday raised the price of retail sugar for sale through its public rationing system to 10.50 rupees per kg from 9.05 rupees in order to cut subsidies, a government spokesman said.

"To reduce the element of subsidy in the distribution of sugar through the public distribution system (PDS), the government of India has decided to fix the retail issue price of sugar to be distributed through the PDS at 10.50 rupees per kg with effect from February 10," he said.
The spokesman did not say how much the government would save.

The Economic Times newspaper said on Monday that the government had been spending six billion rupees each year on levy sugar subsidies. At present the sugar industry sells 40 percent of its production to the government as levy sugar.
United News of India (UNI) said Monday's price revision would reduce the subsidy on levy sugar by about five billion rupees ($170 million).
A Food Ministry statement said the retail issue price of sugar for PDS was fixed at 9.05 rupees in February 1994.
It said since then the minimum price of sugarcane paid to farmers had been raised three times without any corresponding increase in retail sugar prices.
